banner: Inputs: 8 files; prices from <external>/library, rates from <external>/rates

SPX reset dates: last NYSE session of the week / month / quarter from 1970-01-01 (calendar_letf/nyse.py, refuses data that lack it); before that the last row of the period.
NDX early-reset trigger: the NASDAQ:QQQ price (daily low) from 1999-03-10, scaled to the NASDAQ:NDX price index before that; trigger basis 'etf'; drop 35% from the fund's base; fill mode 'level'.
NDX day counts: financing (reference rate and swap spread) ACT/360; expense ratio ACT/365 (calendar days between rows, so weekends and holidays accrue).
NDX reset dates: last NYSE session of the week / month / quarter from 1970-01-01 (calendar_letf/nyse.py, refuses data that lack it); before that the last row of the period.
MODELED: a live fund of this design traded 2024-08-30 to 2025-02-28; no live fund exists today
meta.trigger_base_case: ETF price and daily low from the ETF's first bar (AMEX:SPY 1993-01-29, NASDAQ:QQQ 1999-03-10), index price before

statistics.headline_interval: HEADLINE (R2 step 10): non-overlapping windows of each start phase pooled (step = horizon in months): mean +/- t(df, 0.975) x SE, SE^2 = mean of s_p^2 / k_p, df = smallest k_p - 1; columns indep_*; simulated coverage at every published configuration, and its limit under persistent regimes, in results/coverage_sim.md
statistics.interval: SECONDARY: mean +/- t(k-1, 0.975) x block-bootstrap SE; circular blocks; block = horizon in months; k = n // block; 10,000 resamples; seed 0; columns bb_* (and gap_*, same numbers). Block-bootstrap SE biased low with block = window length: simulated coverage of its 95% intervals 0.85-0.92 (mean) and 0.86-0.93 (median) at the published configurations, against 0.94-1.00 for the phase-pooled interval under independent months (results/coverage_sim.md, which also states the limit under persistent regimes; ASSUMPTIONS section 7).
statistics.median_interval: SECONDARY: median of the window gaps +/- t(k-1, 0.975) x block-bootstrap SE of the median; same blocks, resamples and seed as the mean interval; columns bb_median_* (and median_*, same numbers); a reasonable device, not exact on skewed data; its coverage sits next to the mean's in results/coverage_sim.md
statistics.independent_interval: same as headline_interval (kept under its earlier name)
statistics.noisy: HEADLINE flag: the phase-pooled interval covers zero; noisy_bb_mean / noisy_bb_median: the block-bootstrap interval covers zero (secondary)
statistics.variance_ratio: Lo-MacKinlay (1988) unbiased VR(q), heteroskedasticity-robust z*(q); on simple daily returns of the total-return series
statistics.prediction: Bessembinder second order: -2 x [C(T,2) mu^2 + T sigma^2 / 2 (VR_T - 1)] per period, T = 5 / 21 / 63 days
